head.name: on the network as \\{{ name }}
head.notSetUp: Samba is not set up yet

alerts.adminHint: Without admin mode everything is readable; the buttons ask for admin mode first.
alerts.adminOnly: You can look at everything; changes need admin mode, which your user does not have.

setup.title: Set up Samba
setup.text: The packages are there. Once: add the services to the autostart and start them, write the configuration.
setup.foreign: There is a Samba already: {{ what }}. Its configuration and its user database are kept with .edelweiss-bak; the page starts empty and takes nothing over.
setup.adminFirst: Admin mode shows whether there is a Samba already, before the page changes anything.
setup.adminOnly: Only a user with admin mode can set up Samba.

services.noLocalInterface: No chosen interface is purely local (private IPv4 addresses only); Explorer and Finder do not find the server.

shares.empty: No share yet. Add the first with “Add a share”.
shares.legend: ✎ read and write · 👁 read only · Whoever is not named does not see the share.
shares.unmounted: The disk of “{{ name }}” is not mounted – the share is off until it is back.
shares.orphans: These names have no Samba entry any more (deleted), so they have no access: {{ names }}.

skipped.bad_name: the name does not work for Samba
skipped.case_clash: the name equals another one but for upper and lower case
skipped.bad_path: the folder does not work for Samba

share.name: Name (what it is called on the network)
share.hidden: hidden – shows up in nobody's list, reachable only as {{ address }}
share.owner: Samba accesses the files as the owner of the folder ({{ owner }}); nothing changes in the existing files.
share.ownerPerUser: This share uses folder rights: Samba accesses the files as each user, in the group {{ group }}.
share.ownerRoot: The folder belongs to root. Choose a folder of its own, or make one with “New folder”.
share.ownerMissing: The folder belongs to UID {{ uid }} and GID {{ gid }}, which have no account on this host (a disk from another computer, for example).
share.ownerReading: Reading the owner of the folder …
share.pathHint: Choose a folder on a data disk.
share.pathPerUser: This share uses folder rights and keeps its folder.
share.pathInUse: The folder is inside another share, or holds one: {{ shares }}.
share.nameTaken: There is a share with that name already.
share.noUsers: No Samba users yet – add them in the tab “Users”.
share.nobody: Nobody has access: Samba serves the share once someone has a right.
share.usersUnknown: The Samba users cannot be read right now – reload before you change the share.

rights.deletedNote: no Samba entry any more; goes when saved

navigator.title: Choose a folder
navigator.truncated: There are more folders here than the list shows.
navigator.note: folders only · system folders are not offered · no links
navigator.exists: There is such a folder here already.
navigator.inShare: The share {{ share }} is here: a new folder in it could never be a share of its own.

folders.truncated: There are more folders here than the list shows.
folders.hint: Click a folder to set its rights. Subfolders inherit them as long as they have none of their own.
folders.viewOnly: The tree is there to look at only.
folders.rootMixed: Mixed state in the share itself: not all files have the rights of the share – after a cancel, for example.

folder.title: Rights for “{{ path }}”
folder.note: Rights here can only be narrower than on the share. Whoever has no rights does not see the folder.
folder.noteAbove: Rights here can only be narrower than in the folder above. Whoever has no rights does not see the folder.
folder.root: These are the rights of the share; they are changed when the share is edited.
folder.files: The rights are written to every file and every subfolder (Samba rights only; owner and Linux permissions stay) – that runs as a job with progress, which you can cancel.
folder.inherit: Take the rights of the share
folder.convertTitle: Prepare the share for folder rights
folder.convertText: The existing files of this share are made readable and writable for the group; owner and content stay.
folder.convertFiles: That concerns {{ files }} files and folders.
folder.convertMore: That concerns more than {{ files }} files and folders.
folder.mixed: Mixed state: not all files in this folder have the rights shown here – after a cancel, for example.
folder.partial: The folder is large: only a part of it was checked.
folder.usersUnknown: The Samba users cannot be read right now – reload before you change the rights.
folder.nobody: Nobody has rights on the share that this folder could narrow.
folder.nobodyAbove: Nobody has rights in the folder above that this folder could narrow.

recycle.title: Recycle bin of {{ name }}
recycle.partial: Not everything in the recycle bin could be counted: size and number are a minimum.
recycle.truncated: The list shows the newest {{ n }}.
recycle.conflict: Nothing is overwritten: if a file of the same name is at the former place already, the restored one gets the suffix “(wiederhergestellt)”.
recycle.gone: That is no longer in the recycle bin.
recycle.emptyTitle: Empty the recycle bin of {{ name }}
recycle.emptyText: All files in the recycle bin of {{ name }} are deleted for good. That cannot be undone.

connections.adminOnly: The connections are only visible in admin mode.
connections.note: read again every few seconds while the tab is open

delete.title: Delete the share {{ name }}
delete.text: Only the share goes: the folder {{ path }} and its files stay.

serviceAccount.title: Create a service account
serviceAccount.text: The folder {{ path }} belongs to UID {{ uid }} and GID {{ gid }}, which have no account on this host. The extension creates the service account smb-{{ uid }} with exactly these IDs: no login, no home directory, no Samba user. Nothing changes in the files.
serviceAccount.idNote: The account gets exactly this ID; new users do not get it afterwards.
serviceAccount.exists: The owner of the folder has an account already.

users.empty: No Samba users yet. Add the first with “Add a Samba user”.
users.unknown: The Samba users are only visible in admin mode.
users.extOld: The installed users extension is older than 0.2.0: it does not recognise pure Samba users, does not protect them and does not carry the Samba password along. Update it.
users.unreadable: The Samba users could not be read.

account.name: Name
account.sambaNote: For shares only: no login over SSH, at the console or in edelweiss, no home directory.
account.hostNote: Samba gets the same password. If it changes later in “Users”, Samba follows.
account.noHostUsers: No host user without Samba access.
account.deleteText: The user and their account on this host are deleted.
account.dropText: The Linux account {{ name }} stays; only the access to Samba goes.
account.deleteShares: Their rights in these shares are lost: {{ shares }}.
account.deleteNoShares: They have no rights in any share.
account.syncText: Enter the Linux password; Samba gets the same.
account.jobError: Done, but {{ name }} is still in shares, without access: the job that takes the name out could not start ({{ error }}). Remove it on the page with “Remove orphaned names”.

settings.name: Name on the network
settings.smb2: Allow older devices (SMB2) – e.g. scanners, old printers or Windows 7. Otherwise SMB3 only.
settings.discovery: Show on the network (Windows Explorer and Mac Finder)
settings.notDiscoverable: Samba yes, but not visible in Explorer/Finder
settings.note: Even on a chosen interface Samba only takes connections from private address ranges.

dialog.busy: Another change is running – wait until it is done.

done.folder-convert: {{ share }} is prepared for folder rights; rights for “{{ path }}” set.
done.folder-inherit: “{{ path }}” has the rights from above again.
done.recycle-restore: “{{ name }}” is back in {{ dir }}. If a file of the same name was there already, the restored one is called “{{ conflict }}”.
done.recycle-empty: The recycle bin of {{ name }} is empty.

kinds.user-drop: Remove the user from the shares

job.interrupted: Interrupted: {{ kind }} {{ target }} at step {{ n }}/{{ m }} ({{ label }}). Check the state before you go on.

steps.cleanup: set up the cleanup of the recycle bins
steps.convert: prepare the share for folder rights
steps.discovery: limit WS-Discovery and mDNS to the local networks

jobs.failed: Step {{ n }}/{{ m }} ({{ label }}) failed: {{ error }}
jobs.interrupted: The job was interrupted at step {{ n }}/{{ m }} ({{ label }}). Check the state before you go on.
jobs.cancelled: The job was cancelled at step {{ n }}/{{ m }} ({{ label }}). Steps already done stay done; check the result.
jobs.not_confirmed: Step {{ n }}/{{ m }} ({{ label }}) was not confirmed in time.
jobs.no_noreplace: Step {{ n }}/{{ m }} ({{ label }}): the file system cannot rename safely. Nothing was restored, so that nothing is overwritten.

errors.invalid_input: The input is not valid: {{ message }}
errors.invalid_json: The request could not be read: {{ message }}
errors.length_required: The request had no length – reload the page.
errors.not_setup: Samba is not set up on this host yet – run the setup first.
errors.busy: Another change is running – try again in a moment.
errors.inUseBy: That is still in use by: {{ shares }}.
errors.exists: There is one with that name already.
errors.unavailable: The disk of this share is not there.
errors.unavailableShare: The disk of the share {{ share }} is not there.
errors.no_owner: The owner of the folder has no account on this host – create a service account.
errors.noOwner: The owner {{ uid }}:{{ gid }} of the folder has no account on this host – create a service account.
errors.root_owned: The folder belongs to root. Choose a folder of its own, or make one with “New folder”.
errors.no_acl: The disk of this share cannot keep folder rights.
errors.noAcl: The disk of this share cannot keep folder rights: {{ reason }}
errors.needs_convert: The share has to be prepared for folder rights first.
errors.needsConvert: The share {{ share }} has to be prepared for folder rights first ({{ files }} files and folders).
errors.system_account: That does not work with a system account or an account of the extension.
errors.systemGroup: The group {{ group }} is a group of the system: a service account joins only the group users or a group with a GID of 1000 to 65532.
errors.not_cancellable: That cannot be cancelled right now – the job is in a step that cannot be cancelled, or it is over.
errors.unauthenticated: The session is over. Reload the page and sign in again.
errors.csrf_invalid: The page was open too long. Reload it and try again.

reason.not_absolute: The folder has to be an absolute path without . and .. (like /mnt/data/Photos).
reason.no_data_mount: The folder is on no data disk.
reason.link: The folder is a link or lies behind one – links are not followed.
reason.per_user: This share uses folder rights and keeps its folder.
reason.per_user_disk_changed: This share uses folder rights and is on another disk now. Remove it and add it again.
reason.system_dir: Folders of the system (like /var/lib or /var/log) are not offered and not shared, nor a folder that holds one.
reason.in_share: The folder is in a share: a new folder in it could never be a share of its own.

aclReason.no_xattr: The file system keeps no extended attributes.
aclReason.no_privilege: The extension may not write the rights there (security.* attributes).
aclReason.no_posix_acl: The file system has no POSIX ACLs.

field.name: The name is not valid: {{ message }}
field.path: The folder is not valid: {{ message }}
field.dir: The folder is not valid: {{ message }}
field.folder: The folder in the share is not valid: {{ message }}
field.recycleDays: The recycle bin keeps files 1 to 3650 days.
field.rights: Those rights are not valid: {{ message }}
field.user: The user is not valid: {{ message }}
field.item: There is no such item in the recycle bin: {{ message }}
field.share: The share is missing in the request: {{ message }}
field.kind: There is no such kind of change: {{ message }}
field.settings: The settings are missing in the request: {{ message }}
field.workgroup: The workgroup has 1 to 15 letters, digits, _ and -.
field.interfaces: That interface does not work: {{ message }}
field.password: The password has 1 to 256 bytes, without a line break.
field.uid: The UID of a service account lies in 1000 to 65532: {{ message }}
field.gid: The GID of a service account lies in 1000 to 65532: {{ message }}
